# IParticleBehavior

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Particles` · interface

```csharp
public interface IParticleBehavior
```

Custom code for a particle effect, for what its built-in values don't cover. Set it as the effect's [`ParticleEffect.Behavior`](ParticleEffect.md#behavior).

## Remarks

One instance serves every particle of every effect that uses it, so keep per-particle state in the particle ([`Particle.Custom`](Particle.md#custom), for example). A behavior changes a particle's simulation state while it updates; a [`ParticleRenderer`](ParticleRenderer.md) reads the final drawn state while it draws. A behavior runs in the middle of the system's update, so it must not create emitters, burst or clear the system it belongs to.

## Methods

### Start

```csharp
void Start(ref Particle particle)
```

Types: [`Particle`](Particle.md)

Adjusts a particle as it starts, after the effect's values are applied.

### Update

```csharp
bool Update(ref Particle particle, float elapsedSeconds)
```

Types: [`Particle`](Particle.md)

Adjusts a particle each frame, after the effect has moved it and aged it by `elapsedSeconds`.

**Returns:** False to remove the particle.

To stay correct at any frame rate, change things by rates times `elapsedSeconds`, or compute them from [`Particle.AgeSeconds`](Particle.md#ageseconds).
